problems.title: Two Sum
problems.statement:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. You can return the answer in any order.
commonMistakes: Reusing the same element twice (e.g. nums[i] * 2 === target at index i)
Sorting array without preserving original indices
hints: Can you search for the complement (target - nums[i]) in O(1) time?
A Hash Map allows constant-time lookup for previously seen numbers.
Store the index of each number as you iterate through the array.
Check if target - nums[i] is already in the map before inserting nums[i].

testCases.explanation: Stress test scale N=2002 for complexity verification
Stress test scale N=3002 for complexity verification

problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.statement: Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return `false` if every element is distinct.
commonMistakes: Double loop O(N^2) causing Time Limit Exceeded
hints: A Set stores only unique values.
If you check set.has(x) before inserting x, you detect duplicates immediately.
Early exit on the first duplicate found.

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.statement:
Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s`, and `false` otherwise.

An Anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, typically using all the original letters exactly once.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Edge/boundary case for Valid Anagram testing minimal, empty, or single-element inputs.

commonMistakes: Sorting strings which adds O(N log N) overhead
hints: If s.length !== t.length, they cannot be anagrams.
Use a frequency array of size 26 for English lowercase letters.
Increment count for chars in s, decrement for chars in t.

testCases.explanation: Stress test scale N=2000 for complexity verification
Stress test scale N=2001 for complexity verification

problems.title: Concatenation of Array
problems.statement:
Given an integer array `nums` of length `n`, you want to create an array `ans` of length `2n` where `ans[i] == nums[i]` and `ans[i + n] == nums[i]` for `0 <= i < n` (0-indexed).

Specifically, `ans` is the concatenation of two `nums` arrays.

Return the array `ans`.

examples.explanation: Edge/boundary case for Concatenation of Array testing minimal, empty, or single-element inputs.

commonMistakes: Dynamic re-allocations vs preallocating 2n array
hints: Create an array of size 2 * n.
Set ans[i] and ans[i + n] to nums[i] in a single loop.

testCases.explanation: Stress test scale N=500 for complexity verification
Stress test scale N=1000 for complexity verification

problems.title: Build Array from Permutation
problems.statement:
Given a zero-based permutation `nums` (0-indexed), build an array `ans` of the same length where `ans[i] = nums[nums[i]]` for each `0 <= i < nums.length` and return it.

A zero-based permutation `nums` is an array of distinct integers from `0` to `nums.length - 1` (inclusive).

Can you do it in `O(1)` extra space (in-place)?
constraints: The elements in nums are distinct.

examples.explanation: ans = [nums[0], nums[2], nums[1], nums[5], nums[3], nums[4]].
Edge/boundary case for Build Array from Permutation testing minimal, empty, or single-element inputs.

commonMistakes: Overwriting nums[i] in-place without modulo encoding, corrupting subsequent lookups
hints: In-place trick: store both old and new value in nums[i] using nums[i] + n * (nums[nums[i]] % n).
Then decode by dividing by n.

Stress test scale N=1000 for complexity verification

problems.statement:

problems.title: Richest Customer Wealth
problems.statement:
You are given an `m x n` integer grid `accounts` where `accounts[i][j]` is the amount of money the `i`th customer has in the `j`th bank. Return the wealth that the richest customer has.

A customer's wealth is the amount of money they have in all their bank accounts. The richest customer is the customer that has the maximum wealth.

examples.explanation: Edge/boundary case for Richest Customer Wealth testing minimal, empty, or single-element inputs.

commonMistakes: Summing columns instead of rows
hints: Iterate over each row (customer).
Sum the bank values in each row.
Track the maximum sum seen.

problems.title: Find Pivot Index
problems.statement:
Given an array of integers `nums`, calculate the pivot index of this array.

The pivot index is the index where the sum of all the numbers strictly to the left of the index is equal to the sum of all the numbers strictly to the index's right.

If the index is on the left edge of the array, then the left sum is 0 because there are no elements to the left. This also applies to the right edge of the array.

Return the leftmost pivot index. If no such index exists, return `-1`.
commonMistakes: Recalculating left and right sums in nested loops O(N^2)
hints: First compute total sum of the array in O(N).
As you iterate, rightSum = total - leftSum - nums[i].
If leftSum === rightSum, return current index.

testCases.explanation: Stress test scale N=3000 for complexity verification
Stress test scale N=4000 for complexity verification

problems.title: Plus One
problems.statement:
You are given a large integer represented as an integer array `digits`, where each `digits[i]` is the `i`th digit of the integer. The digits are ordered from most significant to least significant in left-to-right order. The large integer does not contain any leading `0`'s.

Increment the large integer by one and return the resulting array of digits.
constraints: digits does not contain any leading 0's.
commonMistakes: Converting to native Number (overflows for > 16 digits)
hints: Iterate backwards from last digit.
If digit < 9, increment and return.
If digit === 9, set to 0 and continue.
If all digits were 9, prepend 1 to the array.

problems.title: Remove Element
problems.statement:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `val`, remove all occurrences of `val` in `nums` in-place. The order of the elements may be changed. Then return the number of elements in `nums` which are not equal to `val`.

Consider the number of elements in `nums` which are not equal to `val` be `k`. To get accepted, you need to:
- Change the array `nums` such that the first `k` elements of `nums` contain the elements which are not equal to `val`.
- Return `k`.

examples.explanation: Edge/boundary case for Remove Element testing minimal, empty, or single-element inputs.

commonMistakes: Using splice inside loop causing O(N^2) shifting
hints: Maintain write pointer k.
Whenever nums[i] !== val, copy to nums[k] and increment k.

testCases.explanation: Stress test scale N=100 for complexity verification
Stress test scale N=100 for complexity verification

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
problems.statement: Given an integer array `nums` sorted in non-decreasing order, remove the duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears only once. The relative order of the elements should be kept the same. Then return the number of unique elements in `nums`.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.

examples.explanation: Edge/boundary case for Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array testing minimal, empty, or single-element inputs.

commonMistakes: Failing to modify nums in-place
hints: Since nums is sorted, duplicates are adjacent.
Compare nums[i] with nums[i - 1].
Copy new unique elements into nums[write++].

problems.title: Merge Sorted Array
problems.statement:
You are given two integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, sorted in non-decreasing order, and two integers `m` and `n`, representing the number of elements in `nums1` and `nums2` respectively.

Merge `nums1` and `nums2` into a single array sorted in non-decreasing order in-place inside `nums1`.
commonMistakes: Merging from front (which overwrites unread elements in nums1)
hints: Merge backwards from the end (p = m + n - 1).
Compare nums1[p1] and nums2[p2], place largest at nums1[p].
In-place O(1) space.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.statement:
You are given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is the price of a given stock on the `i`th day.

You want to maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy one stock and choosing a different day in the future to sell that stock.

Return the maximum profit you can achieve from this transaction. If you cannot achieve any profit, return `0`.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price = 1) and sell on day 5 (price = 6), profit = 6-1 = 5.
Edge/boundary case for Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock testing minimal, empty, or single-element inputs.

commonMistakes: Trying to sell before buying (nested loop or sorting error)
hints: Track the minimum price seen so far as you iterate.
At each price, potential profit is price - minPrice.
Update maxProfit if higher.

problems.title: Majority Element
problems.statement:
Given an array `nums` of size `n`, return the majority element.

The majority element is the element that appears more than `floor(n / 2)` times. You may assume that the majority element always exists in the array.

hints: Boyer-Moore Voting Algorithm:
Maintain candidate and count.
Increment count if n === candidate, decrement otherwise. If count becomes 0, pick current n as new candidate.

hints: Expected sum of numbers from 0 to n is n * (n + 1) / 2.
Missing number is expectedSum - sum(nums).

problems.title: Single Number
problems.statement:
Given a non-empty array of integers `nums`, every element appears twice except for one. Find that single one.

You must implement a solution with a linear runtime complexity and use only constant extra space.
constraints: Each element in the array appears twice except for one element which appears only once.
commonMistakes: Using Hash Set with O(N) space when XOR achieves O(1) space
hints: XOR properties: a ^ a = 0 and a ^ 0 = a.
XOR is associative and commutative.
XOR-ing all elements cancels duplicates leaving the unique element.

problems.title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
problems.statement:
Given an array `nums` of `n` integers where `nums[i]` is in the range `[1, n]`, return an array of all the integers in the range `[1, n]` that do not appear in `nums`.

Could you do it without extra space and in `O(n)` runtime? You may assume the returned list does not count as extra space.

examples.explanation: Edge/boundary case for Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array testing minimal, empty, or single-element inputs.

commonMistakes: Using Hash Set which uses O(N) auxiliary space instead of in-place negation
hints: Each value v corresponds to index v - 1.
Negate nums[abs(nums[i]) - 1] to mark that the number appeared.
Any index i with nums[i] > 0 was never visited, so i + 1 is missing.

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.statement:
A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward. Alphanumeric characters include letters and numbers.

Given a string `s`, return `true` if it is a palindrome, or `false` otherwise.
constraints: s consists only of printable ASCII characters.

examples.explanation: Empty string after removing non-alphanumeric is a palindrome.

commonMistakes: Creating intermediate cleaned string which violates O(1) space
hints: Use two pointers (left and right) moving toward each other.
Skip non-alphanumeric characters.
Compare lowercase character codes.

problems.title: Reverse String II
problems.statement:
Given a string `s` and an integer `k`, reverse the first `k` characters for every `2k` characters counting from the start of the string.

If there are fewer than `k` characters left, reverse all of them. If there are less than `2k` but greater than or equal to `k` characters, then reverse the first `k` characters and leave the other as original.
constraints: s consists of only lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Edge/boundary case for Reverse String II testing minimal, empty, or single-element inputs.

commonMistakes: Off-by-one when remaining characters are fewer than k
hints: Iterate with step size 2 * k.
For each chunk, reverse the segment from start to min(start + k - 1, length - 1).
